sourcedFrom: ROUGH RIDER SMALL-BORE INSTRUCTION MANUAL GENERAL SAFETY, OPERATING INSTRUCTIONS AND LIMITED WARRANTY — 045-0019-00 Rev 1 (ABSENT — no copyright line is printed in the document.)
cleanIntro: This book is scoped to the SMALL-BORE Rough Rider — the .22 LR / .22 WMR gun — and Heritage prints that bound in the title. If yours is a .357 Big Bore, this is not its manual. Within the small-bore family the gun is still variable and you have to know which one you have: 6-shot and 9-shot cylinders are not interchangeable, and the .22 LR and .22 Magnum cylinders take different ammunition. The published strip is short by design — hammer to the second click, gate open, every chamber checked, base pin lock pressed, base pin out, cylinder out. Heritage says the gun is cleaned and lubricated with no disassembly at all beyond that, and forbids taking the barrel down.

steps.title: Hammer block up, hammer to the second click
steps.action: Point the Rough Rider in a safe direction with your finger outside the trigger guard. Push the hammer block up into the safe position, then pull the hammer back to the SECOND notch — the loading notch — where the cylinder spins freely. Heritage's own before-cleaning list is six items long and this is the first half of it, because on a single action the cylinder will not turn to be inspected until the hammer is at that notch.
steps.prose: The first click is the old safety notch and the cylinder will not turn there. Feel for the second, then check the cylinder spins.
steps.quote: Before cleaning: (1) keep the muzzle pointed in a safe direction, (2) keep your finger off the trigger, (3) keep the hammer block in the up position, (4) pull the hammer back to the second notch (or click), (5) open loading gate, and (6) rotate the cylinder clockwise and check every chamber to be sure it is empty.
steps.cite: ROUGH RIDER SMALL-BORE INSTRUCTION MANUAL GENERAL SAFETY, OPERATING INSTRUCTIONS AND LIMITED WARRANTY — 045-0019-00 Rev 1 — Care and Maintenance, p.25
steps.warn: NEVER ATTEMPT TO DISASSEMBLE OR CLEAN A LOADED FIREARM. DOING SO CAN RESULT IN SERIOUS BODILY INJURY OR DEATH.

steps.title: Gate open, every chamber checked by eye
steps.action: Open the loading gate and rotate the cylinder clockwise, looking through the gate at EVERY chamber in turn. Six or nine of them, all of them, one at a time. If any are loaded, line each chamber up with the ejector rod and push the cartridge out, then go round again and double-check that all are empty.
steps.prose: A .22 case sitting low in a chamber is easy to miss in poor light. Turning the cylinder past a chamber you did not actually look into is how this goes wrong.
steps.caution: If you experience difficulty in unloading your Rough Rider, STOP! Make certain the hammer block is in the up (safe) position.
steps.quote: 5. Line up the chamber with the ejector rod, and push out the cartridge. Line up the next chamber and repeat this until all chambers are unloaded. Be sure to double check that all chambers are empty.
steps.cite: ROUGH RIDER SMALL-BORE INSTRUCTION MANUAL GENERAL SAFETY, OPERATING INSTRUCTIONS AND LIMITED WARRANTY — 045-0019-00 Rev 1 — Unloading, p.19

steps.title: SMALL-BORE only — this is not the Big Bore book
steps.action: Check the title on your own manual before you follow any of this. Heritage publishes the Rough Rider in a small-bore .22 LR / .22 WMR form and separately as a Big Bore in centrefire chamberings, and this book scopes itself to the small-bore in its own title. The cylinders, the ammunition rules and the capacities below are the rimfire gun's.
steps.prose: A .357 Rough Rider is a different frame size with a different cylinder and a different ammunition table. Nothing here transfers to it.
steps.caution: Small-bore .22 LR / .22 WMR only. A Big Bore Rough Rider is outside this manual.
steps.cite: ROUGH RIDER SMALL-BORE INSTRUCTION MANUAL GENERAL SAFETY, OPERATING INSTRUCTIONS AND LIMITED WARRANTY — 045-0019-00 Rev 1 — Cover, p.1

steps.title: Base pin lock pressed, base pin out
steps.action: With every chamber confirmed empty, press the base pin lock nut in on the left of the frame and pull the base pin forward out of the frame at the same time. The lock nut has to stay pressed through the whole pull — release it halfway and the pin catches on its detent, which feels like the pin is seized when it is not.
steps.prose: The base pin is the axle the cylinder turns on. It slides out the front, past the ejector tube, so keep the gun level.
steps.quote: 4. Press the base pin lock nut while pulling the base pin out of the frame. (Fig. 1)
steps.cite: ROUGH RIDER SMALL-BORE INSTRUCTION MANUAL GENERAL SAFETY, OPERATING INSTRUCTIONS AND LIMITED WARRANTY — 045-0019-00 Rev 1 — Changing Cylinders, p.23
steps.warn: Never remove or install a loaded cylinder. If dropped or struck on a hard surface, the ammunition can fire.

steps.title: Cylinder out through the gate side
steps.action: With the base pin clear, push the cylinder out of the frame from left to right — out through the open loading gate side. It lifts straight out with nothing else holding it. That is the whole of the published strip: frame, base pin, cylinder.
steps.prose: Heritage's own cable-lock instructions use the same sequence, which is a useful confirmation you are doing it the way the factory intends.
steps.quote: 6. Push the cylinder out of frame from left to right.
steps.cite: ROUGH RIDER SMALL-BORE INSTRUCTION MANUAL GENERAL SAFETY, OPERATING INSTRUCTIONS AND LIMITED WARRANTY — 045-0019-00 Rev 1 — To Install the Factory-Supplied Locking Device, p.14

steps.title: Which cylinder is in your gun
steps.action: Look at the cylinder you have just taken out before you clean it or swap it. The two cylinders are not interchangeable in what they will fire, and on the Rough Rider family the 6-shot and 9-shot cylinders will only work in the gun built for them. Fitting the wrong one, or feeding a .22 Magnum cylinder rimfire long rifle, is outside what Heritage permits.
steps.prose: Mark them if you own both. They look alike in a cleaning tray.
steps.caution: 7. Only .22 WMR ammo can be fired in the .22 Magnum Cylinder.
steps.quote: 6. The following ammunition can be fired in the Long Rifle Cylinder: .22 L.R., .22 Long, .22 Short, .22 CB (in cap, short, long, and long rifle lengths), .22 BB (in cap, short, and long lengths).
steps.cite: ROUGH RIDER SMALL-BORE INSTRUCTION MANUAL GENERAL SAFETY, OPERATING INSTRUCTIONS AND LIMITED WARRANTY — 045-0019-00 Rev 1 — Changing Cylinders, p.23

steps.title: Bore, then the areas the gas reaches
steps.action: Clean the bore and everything the powder residue touches with an appropriate brush — the forcing cone, the cylinder face, the chambers and the frame around the barrel/cylinder gap. If you find lead in the barrel, scrub it with a brass brush drenched in oil. Rimfire lead builds in the forcing cone faster than anywhere else and a leaded cone hurts accuracy long before it hurts function.
steps.prose: Heritage's shooting-session limit is 200 rounds: past that, clean it before shooting further.
steps.aside: When shooting more than 200 rounds in a row, your firearm should be cleaned before further shooting.
steps.quote: 5. For cleaning after shooting, all powder residues should be removed from the barrel and other adjacent areas subject to such deposits, with appropriate brush.
steps.cite: ROUGH RIDER SMALL-BORE INSTRUCTION MANUAL GENERAL SAFETY, OPERATING INSTRUCTIONS AND LIMITED WARRANTY — 045-0019-00 Rev 1 — Care and Maintenance, p.24

steps.title: A thin oil film, and the excess wiped off
steps.action: Wipe the metal down with a lightly oiled cloth and do the same through the bore. Then take the excess off — Heritage wants a thin protecting film left, not a wet gun. Get the dust out of the crevices with a small clean brush while it is apart.
steps.prose: Excess oil on a rimfire single action runs into the chambers and contaminates the next rounds. A film is protection; a puddle is a misfire.
steps.caution: Avoid the use of cloth holsters or any other moisture retaining material.
steps.quote: 3. To keep a gun in good condition, it must be kept clean and covered with a light film of good quality gun oil to prevent corrosion. This is especially necessary after use.
steps.cite: ROUGH RIDER SMALL-BORE INSTRUCTION MANUAL GENERAL SAFETY, OPERATING INSTRUCTIONS AND LIMITED WARRANTY — 045-0019-00 Rev 1 — Care and Maintenance, p.24

steps.title: Stop where Heritage stops
steps.action: Do not go further. Heritage states that the gun is cleaned and lubricated under normal conditions with no disassembly at all, tells you outright not to disassemble the barrel, and sends any repair-level teardown to the factory or a qualified gunsmith. The warranty also excludes damage from failing to follow the disassembly instructions in this manual.
steps.prose: There is no published hand, bolt or spring work for this revolver, and the internals of a single-action are under spring tension behind the grip frame.
steps.quote: 1. The firearm may be cleaned and lubricated under normal conditions without the need of any disassembly. Do not disassemble the barrel. 2. In special conditions, such as repairs, when disassembly is necessary, it is recommended the firearm be returned to the factory or sent to a qualified gunsmith.
steps.cite: ROUGH RIDER SMALL-BORE INSTRUCTION MANUAL GENERAL SAFETY, OPERATING INSTRUCTIONS AND LIMITED WARRANTY — 045-0019-00 Rev 1 — Care and Maintenance, p.24

steps.title: Field strip complete
steps.action: Frame, base pin and cylinder. That is the entire published strip for the Rough Rider and Heritage draws the line immediately after it — the gun is designed to be cleaned in this state. Put the cylinder back in, run the base pin home until the lock nut clicks, and check the cylinder turns freely at the loading notch.
steps.prose: Anything past this goes to the factory or a gunsmith by the manufacturer's own instruction.
steps.quote: 1. The firearm may be cleaned and lubricated under normal conditions without the need of any disassembly. Do not disassemble the barrel. 2. In special conditions, such as repairs, when disassembly is necessary, it is recommended the firearm be returned to the factory or sent to a qualified gunsmith.
steps.cite: ROUGH RIDER SMALL-BORE INSTRUCTION MANUAL GENERAL SAFETY, OPERATING INSTRUCTIONS AND LIMITED WARRANTY — 045-0019-00 Rev 1 — Care and Maintenance, p.24

deepAbsentReason: Heritage publishes NO deeper procedure for this revolver. Its Care and Maintenance section states in its own words that the firearm is cleaned and lubricated under normal conditions without the need of any disassembly, instructs the owner not to disassemble the barrel, and directs that where disassembly IS necessary — repairs — the gun be returned to the factory or sent to a qualified gunsmith (p.24). The warranty separately excludes 'failure to follow the disassembly instructions in the Heritage Manufacturing, Inc. manual'. There is nothing published beyond dropping the base pin and removing the cylinder, which the field strip already covers, and inventing a lockwork teardown for a single-action revolver under spring tension would be substitution.

cleaning.name: BORE & FORCING CONE
tasks: Brush all powder residue from the barrel and the areas around it
Lead in the barrel: brass brush drenched in oil
Clean the forcing cone and the frame around the barrel/cylinder gap
Clean before shooting further if you have fired more than 200 rounds in a row

cleaning.name: CYLINDER
tasks: Brush each chamber and the cylinder face
Clean the base pin and the base pin bore in the cylinder
Never remove or install a loaded cylinder
Keep the .22 LR and .22 Magnum cylinders identified — they are not interchangeable in what they fire

cleaning.name: FRAME & PROTECTION
tasks: Wipe the metal with a lightly oiled cloth, then remove the excess and leave a thin film
Dust out of every crevice with a small clean brush
Do NOT disassemble the barrel or the lockwork
Store away from moisture-retaining material — no cloth holsters

reassembly: Slide the cylinder back into the frame from right to left, lining its bore up with the base pin hole.
Push the base pin in through the frame and the cylinder until the base pin lock nut clicks and holds it.
Tug the base pin forward to confirm the lock has caught before anything else.
With the hammer at the second notch, spin the cylinder and check it turns freely and indexes.
Lower the hammer on an empty chamber and put the hammer block back up into the safe position.
fncheck: With the revolver empty, pull the hammer to the second notch and confirm the cylinder spins freely and indexes cleanly to each chamber. Tug the base pin forward to prove the lock nut has engaged — a base pin that walks out under recoil frees the cylinder. Cock the hammer fully, flip the hammer block down and dry fire on an empty chamber, checking the hammer falls and the cylinder is locked at that moment. Then put the hammer block back up and leave an empty chamber under the hammer: never carry it with a live round under the hammer and firing pin.
